title: Agreement of one step on a truncated input
statement: Let $M$ be a nondeterministic machine with $k$ work tapes, symbol alphabet $\Gamma$, state set $S$, and input word $x$. Let $m$ be a natural number, $b$ a choice bit, and $c$ a configuration on $x$. Let $c'$ be a configuration on the prefix of $x$ of length at most $m$. Suppose that $c$ and $c'$ have equal states, equal input-head positions, equal work tapes, equal work-tape head positions, and equal outputs, and that the input-head position of $c$ is at most $m$. Then after one step under choice $b$, these five components still agree between the two runs; also, the input-head position after stepping from $c$ is at most its previous position plus one.
